One day, she went for a walk in the woods. Suddenly, she heard a tiny meow. The little girl looked around and saw a tiny kitten stuck in a tree. The kitten was in trouble and she needed help.

The little girl carried the kitten home where she gave it lots of love and care. The kitten was very happy and the little girl named her "Princess". She even found a pretty crown for Princess to wear!
Now, Princess was a very quiet kitty who always loved to be with the little girl. They were best friends forever and always had fun together. The little girl was very proud that she had been brave enough to rescue Princess.

Billy agreed to the operation. Mr. T took two soft shells and put them on Billy's claws. Now, when Billy played with his friends, he couldn't pinch them anymore. Everyone was happy and had fun playing together.

Ben comes closer and smells it. He makes a face. "Yuck, Sara, that is rot. It is old and bad. It was once a fruit, but now it is not good. Throw it away."
Sara drops the rot and wipes her hand on her dress. She sees something shiny under the leaves. She picks it up. It is a metal thing with a round part and a long part. She turns the round part and hears a click.
"What is that, Sara?" Ben says. He is curious.
Sara does not know. She thinks it is a toy. She points the long part at a tree and turns the round part again. A loud bang makes them jump. A hole appears in the tree.
"Wow, Sara, what did you do?" Ben says. He is scared.
Sara is scared too. She drops the metal thing and runs to Ben. They hug each other. They hear a voice from the house.
"Sara, Ben, what was that noise?" It is Mom. She sounds angry.
Sara and Ben look at each other. They do not want to tell Mom. They do not want to get in trouble. They run to the house and hide under the bed. They hope Mom will not find the metal thing. They hope it will rot in the deep hole they dug.

Her mom nods and says, "Yes, you can. But first, you have to clean up the mess he made. And then, you have to play with him and give him some treats. That will make him happy and he will not do it again."

Lisa says, "Fluffy, I am sorry. I was wrong to punish you. You are my pet and I love you. Will you forgive me?"

"Tom, what is wrong?" Sam asks.

Sam laughs. "That is not a cow, that is Daisy. She is nice. She likes to eat corn. She will not hurt you."
Tom is still scared. He does not like Daisy. He wants to go home.
"Can we go home, please?" Tom asks.
"OK, let's go home. I am sorry you are scared. Next time we can play somewhere else." Sam says.
They hold hands and walk out of the corn. They say goodbye to Daisy. They go home. They are still friends.

"Wow, this is the best rock ever!" Lily said. Just then, a tiny voice spoke, "Please put me down!"
Lily looked around, but saw no one. "Who said that?" she asked. The tiny voice said, "It's me, the rock! I'm not a rock, I'm a fairy!"
Lily was very surprised. She had never met a fairy before. She gently put the fairy down on a leaf. The fairy thanked her and said, "For being kind, I will give you a wish."
Lily thought for a moment and said, "I wish for a big bag of pretty rocks!" The fairy waved her tiny hand, and a big bag of rocks appeared. Lily thanked the fairy and went home with her new rocks, happy and amazed by her unexpected adventure.

He thought and thought. The sailor had an idea. He blew a big wind at the cloud. The cloud started to disappear. The water became clean and the fish were happy. The sailor felt good that he helped the fish.

Tom put the sour apple in the little red wagon. He pulled the wagon to a big tree. He dug a hole under the tree and put the sour apple in the hole. Then, he covered the hole with dirt. He felt happy that he buried the sour apple.
After some time, a beautiful apple tree grew in the place where Tom buried the sour apple. The tree had sweet apples, not sour ones. Tom shared the sweet apples with his friends. Everyone loved the sweet apples from the tree. The moral of the story is that good things can come from something we don't like.

Molly slowly nodded and Sam smiled. He reached out his hand and asked if she wanted to hold it. Molly's face lit up and she took it.
Then they continued on their walk, hand in hand. They talked about the birds and plants they could see. Molly laughed often and every now and then she would nod along as Sam talked. 
Sam smiled whenever he saw Molly's eyes light up. When they reached the end of the path, Sam said, “It's been so nice walking with you today.” Molly smiled, nodded, and waved goodbye. 
And then they went their separate ways, with happy memories of their special day.

Sara was sad. She missed her mom. Her mom went to work and Sara stayed with grandma. Grandma was nice, but Sara wanted her mom.
"Grandma, can I have some fruit?" Sara asked. She liked fruit. Fruit was sweet and juicy.
"Sure, Sara. What fruit do you want?" Grandma said. She opened the fridge and showed Sara the fruit.
Sara saw apples, bananas, oranges and grapes. She wanted grapes. Grapes were small and purple. She could eat many grapes.
"I want grapes, please," Sara said. She reached for the grapes.
"Okay, Sara. Here you go. But be careful. Some grapes are hard. They have seeds inside. You have to spit out the seeds. Do you understand?" Grandma said. She gave Sara a bowl of grapes.
Sara nodded. She understood. She took a grape and put it in her mouth. She bit the grape. It was hard. She felt a seed. She spit out the seed. She made a face.
"Yuck! I don't like hard grapes. I like soft grapes," Sara said. She put down the grape.
Grandma smiled. She picked up a grape and squeezed it. It was soft. She gave it to Sara.
"Here, Sara. Try this one. This one is soft. It has no seeds. You will like it," Grandma said.
Sara took the grape and put it in her mouth. She bit the grape. It was soft. It had no seed. It was sweet and juicy. She liked it.
"Mmm! I like soft grapes. Thank you, Grandma," Sara said. She smiled and ate more grapes.
Grandma hugged Sara. She was happy. She loved Sara.
"You're welcome, Sara. I love you. And you know what? Your mom loves you too. She will be back soon. She misses you too," Grandma said.
Sara hugged Grandma. She was happy too. She loved Grandma. And she loved her mom.
"I love you, Grandma. And I love mom. I miss mom. But I'm glad you're here with me," Sara said.
The end.

Lila and Ben were friends. They liked to play with toys and share snacks. One day, they found a big jug in the yard. It was shiny and had a handle and a spout.
"Wow, look at this jug!" Lila said. "It is so pretty! I want to play with it!"
"Me too!" Ben said. "Let's fill it with water and pour it on the flowers!"
They took the jug to the faucet and filled it with water. Then they ran to the flower bed and took turns pouring water on the flowers. They laughed and had fun.
But then, Lila saw a sticker on the bottom of the jug. It said: "This jug is very old and very valuable. Do not touch or break it. It belongs to Mr. Jones."
"Uh-oh," Lila said. "This jug is not a toy. It is very important. We should not play with it. We should give it back to Mr. Jones."
"Who is Mr. Jones?" Ben asked.
"He is the old man who lives next door. He is not very friendly. He always yells at us when we go near his fence. He has a lot of old things in his house. He likes them very much."
"Then we should keep the jug. It is more fun than his old things. He will not miss it. He has too many," Ben said.
"No, Ben. That is not nice. We should not take things that are not ours. We should value what we have and respect what others have. Come on, let's go and say sorry to Mr. Jones and give him back his jug."
But Ben did not want to go. He liked the jug too much. He wanted to keep it for himself. He grabbed the jug from Lila and ran away.
"Ben, stop! Come back!" Lila shouted. "You are being selfish and mean!"
But Ben did not listen. He ran faster and faster. He did not see the rock on the ground. He tripped and fell. The jug flew out of his hands and smashed on the pavement. It broke into many pieces.
Lila ran to Ben and saw the broken jug. She felt very sad and scared. She knew Mr. Jones would be very angry. She also saw that Ben had scraped his knee and elbow. He was bleeding and crying.
"Ben, are you okay?" Lila asked. "I'm sorry you got hurt. But you should not have taken the jug. It was wrong. Now we are in big trouble."
Ben looked at Lila and the broken jug. He realized he had made a big mistake. He wished he had listened to Lila. He wished he had been more friendly and more careful. He wished he could fix the jug and make everything better. But he could not. He had lost a friend and a jug. He felt very sorry and very stupid. He did not know what to do. He wished he could hide. But he could not. He had to face Mr. Jones and his anger. He was very afraid. He knew he would get a bad ending.

Ben and Lily were playing in the yard. They liked to dig in the dirt and make mud pies. They had a big bucket of water to make the mud wet.
"Look, I made a house for my toy car!" Ben said, showing Lily his mud pie. "It has a door and a window and a roof."
"That's nice, Ben," Lily said. "But I can make a bigger house. Watch me!" She poured more water into the dirt and started to make a bigger mud pie.
Ben did not like that. He wanted to have the biggest house. He poured more water into his dirt and made his mud pie bigger too. "Ha! My house is bigger than yours now!" he said.
Lily did not like that. She poured more water into her dirt and made her mud pie bigger too. "No, my house is bigger than yours!" she said.
They kept pouring more water and making their mud pies bigger and bigger. They did not notice that the sky was getting dark and the wind was blowing hard. They did not hear their mom calling them to come inside.
Soon, it started to rain. The rain was heavy and fast. It made the mud pies wetter and wetter. The mud pies started to fall apart. The water started to increase in the yard. It made a big puddle that covered the grass and the flowers.
Ben and Lily looked at their mud pies. They were not houses anymore. They were just lumps of wet mud. They felt sad and mad. They had worked hard to make their houses, but the rain ruined them.
They heard their mom calling them again. "Ben! Lily! Come inside now! It's raining too much!" she said.
They ran to the house. They were wet and dirty. They left their bucket and their toy car in the yard. They did not want to play with them anymore.
Their mom gave them towels and dry clothes. She hugged them and said, "I'm sorry your mud pies got ruined. But you can make new ones another day. Maybe you can make them together and share them. That would be more fun, don't you think?"
Ben and Lily nodded. They felt a little better. They decided to play with their blocks instead. They made a house with their blocks. It had a door and a window and a roof. It was not a big house, but it was a nice house. They put their toy car inside. They smiled at each other. They were happy.

"I don't know," Mia said. "It looks dark and scary. What if there are monsters or bats?"
"Don't be afraid," Tom said. "We can number the steps we take, so we can find our way back. I have a flashlight, too. Come on, it will be fun."
Mia agreed, but she was still nervous. They held hands and walked into the cave. They counted one, two, three, four, five steps. The cave was cold and quiet. They saw some rocks and some bugs, but nothing else.
"Let's go deeper," Tom said. "Maybe there is a treasure or a secret."
"OK, but not too far," Mia said. They counted six, seven, eight, nine, ten steps. The cave was darker and louder. They heard some water and some wind, but nothing else.
"Let's go back," Mia said. "I don't like it here. It's too spooky."
"OK, OK," Tom said. "Let's go back. We can number the steps again, so we don't get lost."
They turned around and walked back. They counted ten, nine, eight, seven, six steps. But then, they saw something that made them stop. It was a big bear, blocking the way out. It was growling and showing its teeth. It looked angry and hungry.
Tom and Mia were very nervous. They did not know what to do. They screamed and hugged each other. They wished they never went into the cave. They hoped someone would hear them and help them. They hoped the bear would go away. They hoped they would be safe.

Tom did not listen. He took his cane and went near the fire. He waved his cane like a magic wand, but the cane got too close to the fire. The cane started to burn. Tom was scared and called his dad for help.
His dad quickly put out the fire on the cane. He said, "Tom, I told you fire is serious. You must always listen and be careful." Tom learned his lesson and promised to be more careful next time.
The moral of the story is to always listen to your parents and be careful, because they know what is best for you.

Leo was a lion who liked to roar. He roared when he was happy, he roared when he was angry, he roared when he was bored. He roared so much that the other animals in the jungle were afraid of him. They ran away when they heard him roar, and they hid in their homes.
One day, Leo was thirsty. He walked to the river to drink some water. He saw a big, shiny fish swimming in the water. He thought the fish looked tasty, so he roared at it. The fish did not run away. It looked at Leo and said, "Why are you roaring at me? I am not afraid of you."
Leo was surprised. He had never met an animal that was not afraid of his roar. He roared louder, hoping to scare the fish. The fish did not move. It said, "You can roar all you want, but you cannot catch me. I am in the water, and you are on the land. You are a lion, and I am a fish. We are different."
Leo was curious. He had never met an animal that was so unusual. He asked the fish, "What is your name? Where do you come from? How do you live in the water?"
The fish smiled. It said, "My name is Finn. I come from the sea. I live in the water by breathing through my gills and swimming with my fins. I can show you, if you want."
Leo wanted to see. He followed Finn into the water. He felt the water on his fur and his paws. He tried to breathe, but he could not. He tried to swim, but he could not. He realized he had made a mistake. He was a lion, and he did not belong in the water. He wanted to go back to the land, but he could not. He was too deep, and he was too weak. He looked at Finn, and he saw a smirk. He understood that Finn had tricked him. He wanted to roar, but he could not. He was silent.

Lily looked at the board and saw that Ben was right. She was in trouble. She did not want to lose. She had an idea. She quickly took her king and replaced it with her queen. She hoped Ben would not notice.
"Hey!" Ben said, looking at the board again. "That's not fair! You can't replace your king with your queen! That's cheating!"
Lily pretended to be confused. "What do you mean? That's my king. See, it has a crown."
Ben shook his head. "No, it doesn't. That's your queen. It has a pointy hat. Your king has a cross. You are stupid!"
Lily felt bad. She knew Ben was right. She was stupid. She had tried to cheat and got caught. She did not want to play chess anymore. She said sorry to Ben and gave him back his horse. She asked him to teach her how to play better.
Ben smiled. He was not angry anymore. He liked to teach Lily. He said it was okay and showed her how to move her king. They played chess again and had fun. They learned from each other and became better players. They thanked their dad for the game and hugged each other. They were not stupid. They were smart.

Tom is a boy. He likes to learn new things. He goes to school with his friends. His teacher is Miss Lily. She is nice and smart. She teaches Tom and his friends many things.
One day, Miss Lily teaches Tom and his friends about animals. She shows them pictures of different animals. She says their names and sounds. Tom and his friends repeat after her.
"This is a cat. It says meow. Can you say meow?" Miss Lily asks.
"Meow!" Tom and his friends say.
"Good! This is a dog. It says woof. Can you say woof?" Miss Lily asks.
"Woof!" Tom and his friends say.
"Very good! This is a cow. It says moo. Can you say moo?" Miss Lily asks.
"Moo!" Tom and his friends say.
Miss Lily shows them more animals. She shows them a bird, a fish, a lion, a monkey, and a snake. Tom and his friends learn their names and sounds. They have fun.
But there is one boy who does not have fun. His name is Ben. He is crazy. He does not like to learn. He likes to make noise and trouble. He does not listen to Miss Lily. He does not say the animal sounds. He says other things.
When Miss Lily shows the cat, Ben says "Quack!"
When Miss Lily shows the dog, Ben says "Oink!"
When Miss Lily shows the cow, Ben says "Baa!"
Miss Lily is confused. She asks Ben why he says the wrong sounds. Ben laughs. He thinks he is funny. He does not care.
Tom and his friends are not happy. They think Ben is rude. They want to learn. They tell Ben to stop. But Ben does not stop. He keeps saying the wrong sounds.
Miss Lily is sad. She does not know what to do. She tries to teach Ben the right sounds. But Ben does not listen. He says more wrong sounds.
When Miss Lily shows the bird, Ben says "Moo!"
When Miss Lily shows the fish, Ben says "Woof!"
When Miss Lily shows the lion, Ben says "Meow!"

"Look at my dragon!" Ben said. "It is big and strong and scary!"
Lily was not scared of the dragon. She thought it was silly and ugly. She wanted to play with her doll. She said, "Your dragon is not real. It is fake and dumb. My doll is real and pretty. She can talk and sing and dance."
Ben was angry. He did not like Lily's doll. He thought it was boring and girly. He said, "Your doll is not real. It is fake and stupid. My dragon can eat your doll and spit out her hair."
Lily was angry too. She did not like Ben's dragon. She said, "No, it can't. Your dragon is made of plastic and cloth. It can't do anything. Watch this!"
Lily grabbed the dragon from Ben's hands and tore its wing. She threw it on the floor and said, "Ha! Now your dragon can't fly. It is broken and useless."
Ben cried. He loved his dragon. He picked it up and hugged it. He said, "You are mean, Lily. You broke my dragon. I hate you."
Lily felt bad. She saw Ben's tears and heard his sobs. She remembered that he was her brother and she loved him. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I didn't mean to break your dragon. I was mad and I did a bad thing. Can you forgive me?"
Ben looked at Lily. He saw her eyes and heard her voice. He remembered that she was his sister and he loved her. He said, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. I was mad too and I said mean things. Can we be friends again?"
Lily nodded. She smiled and said, "Yes, we can. I'm sorry for calling your dragon fake and dumb. It is a nice dragon. Can I play with it?"
Ben nodded. He smiled and said, "Yes, you can. I'm sorry for calling your doll fake and stupid. It is a pretty doll. Can I play with it?"
Lily and Ben hugged and said, "I love you." They shared their toys and played together. They forgot about their fight and had fun. The dragon and the doll were happy too. They were not real, but they felt real. They had friends who cared for them.

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to play in the forest. They liked to look for animals and flowers and mushrooms. One day, they saw a big red mushroom with white spots. It looked like a hat.
"Wow, look at this mushroom!" Sara said. "It is so pretty and big. Can we pick it?"
Tom shook his head. "No, we can't. Mama said some mushrooms are bad. They can make us sick or hurt us. We have to listen to Mama."
Sara pouted. "But I want to touch it. It is so soft and smooth. Please, Tom, let me touch it. Just a little bit."
Tom sighed. He loved his sister and wanted to make her happy. He looked around and saw no one. He thought maybe it was okay to touch the mushroom for a second. He said, "Okay, Sara, you can touch it. But be gentle. Don't break it or pull it. And don't put it in your mouth or nose or eyes. Just touch it with your finger."
Sara smiled. She reached out her hand and touched the mushroom. It felt like velvet. She rubbed it with her finger. She liked it. She wanted to touch it more. She forgot what Tom said. She grabbed the mushroom and pulled it. It came off the ground. She held it in her hand. She brought it close to her face. She smelled it. It smelled sweet. She licked it. It tasted good. She bit it. Just then, he met a thoughtful turtle who was exploring a nearby reef. The shark approached the turtle with a smile.
"Hi turtle friend. What are you doing today?" asked the shark.
The turtle looked up and smiled. "I am exploring the coral reef," he replied.
The shark thought for a moment and then said, "I'm gonna joke that you're too slow to catch anything!"
The turtle laughed. "Ha-ha. That's a funny joke. I'm glad you used your words to be so thoughtful," said the turtle.
The shark and the turtle said goodbye and went their separate ways. That day, the shark learned that it is important to be thoughtful when you joke around.

Tom and Lily liked to play in the attic. They found many old things there, like books, toys, and clothes. One day, they saw a big box with a red label that said "Zoom". They opened the box and found a shiny car with four wheels and a button.
"Wow, look at this!" Tom said. "It must be a zoom car. Let's try it!"
He pushed the button and the car started to make a loud noise. It moved very fast on the floor, zooming around the attic. Tom and Lily laughed and chased the car.
But the car was too fast and too noisy. It bumped into the walls, the shelves, and the boxes. It knocked down some books and toys. It tore some clothes. It made a big mess.
"Stop, stop!" Lily said. "It's breaking everything!"
But Tom did not listen. He liked the zoom car too much. He wanted to keep playing with it.
Suddenly, the car zoomed towards a small window. It crashed through the glass and flew out of the attic. Tom and Lily heard a loud splash.
They ran to the window and looked outside. They saw the car sinking in the pond.
"Oh no!" Tom said. "The zoom car is gone!"
He felt very sad and sorry. He wished he had listened to Lily. He wished he had been more careful with the old things in the attic.
He learned a lesson that day. He learned that zooming is not always fun. He learned that some things are better left alone. He learned that he should respect the past and the present.

Coco looks at the ruler and says, "Measure? What is measure?"
Anna says, "Measure is when you see how long or how tall something is. Look, this ruler has numbers. They tell you how many inches something is. I want to see how many inches you are."
Coco says, "Inches? What are inches?"
Anna says, "Inches are these little lines on the ruler. See, one, two, three, four, and so on. Each line is one inch. If you are five inches long, that means you are as long as five lines."
Coco says, "Oh, I see. Can I measure you too?"
Anna says, "Sure, you can measure me too. But first, let me measure you. Hold still, Coco."
Anna puts the ruler next to Coco's body and counts the lines. She says, "Coco, you are eight inches long. That's very big for a parrot. You are a big, green, smart parrot."
Coco says, "Thank you, Anna. You are a good, kind, pretty girl. Now, can I measure you?"
Anna says, "Okay, Coco. You can measure me. But you have to be careful. Don't peck me with your beak."
Coco says, "Don't worry, Anna. I won't peck you. I love you."

Anna says, "Thank you, Coco. You are very good at measuring. You are a clever, funny, happy parrot."
Coco says, "You are welcome, Anna. You are very good at teaching. You are a smart, nice, happy girl."

Her mom saw her running and asked what happened. Lily told her about the rhinoceros. Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. Rhinoceroses are safe. They won't hurt you if you don't hurt them." 
Lily felt better and went back to the park. She saw the rhinoceros again and remembered what her mom said. She stood still and watched the rhinoceros walk by. 
Lily learned that sometimes things can be scary, but if you stay calm and repeat what you know is true, you can be safe.

"Go away, dog!" Tom says. "This is our ball!"
But the dog does not listen. It grabs the ball in its mouth and runs away. Tom and Jen chase the dog. They want their ball back.
They follow the dog to a big house. The house has a fence and a gate. The dog goes inside the gate. Tom and Jen stop at the gate. They see a sign on the fence. The sign says: "Beware of the dog!"
"Uh-oh," Jen says. "This is the dog's house. Maybe we should not go in."
But Tom is brave. He wants his ball. He opens the gate and goes in. Jen follows him. They look for the dog and the ball.

Tom and Jen say thank you. They take their ball and run out of the gate. They are happy to have their ball back. They are also happy to be away from Rex.
They go back to the park. They look at the sky. The sun is high. It is noon.
"Let's go home," Jen says. "It is time for lunch."
"OK," Tom says. "But let's not play with the ball anymore. Let's play with something else."
They agree. They do not want to see Rex again. They have learned their lesson. They walk home, holding hands. They are still friends.

Lily and Ben were playing in their room. It was very hot outside, so they turned on the fan. The fan made a nice sound and blew cool air on them. They felt comfortable and happy.
They decided to play a game with the fan. They took turns hiding behind the fan and saying "boo!" to each other. They laughed and had fun. Then Lily had an idea. She said to Ben, "Let's make the fan disappear!"
Ben was curious. He asked, "How do we do that?" Lily said, "We need a big sheet. We can cover the fan with the sheet and then pull it off. The fan will be gone!"
They found a big sheet in the closet and brought it to the fan. They carefully draped the sheet over the fan, making sure it was covered. Then they stepped back and counted to three. "One, two, three!" they shouted and pulled the sheet off.
But the fan was still there. It was spinning and blowing air as before. Lily and Ben were confused. They looked at each other and said, "What happened? Why didn't the fan disappear?"
They didn't know that their mom had seen them playing with the sheet and the fan. She thought they might get hurt or break the fan, so she came into the room and unplugged the fan before they pulled the sheet off. She was hiding behind the door, smiling and watching them.
She decided to join their game and have some fun. She plugged the fan back in and waited for them to cover it again. When they did, she quickly unplugged it and moved it to another corner of the room. Then she plugged it in again and hid behind the door.
Lily and Ben pulled the sheet off again and gasped. The fan was gone! They looked around the room and saw it in a different place. They couldn't believe it. They said, "Wow! The fan did disappear! How did it do that?"
They heard their mom giggle behind the door. They realized she was playing with them. They ran to the door and opened it. They saw their mom holding the plug and smiling. They said, "Mom! You made the fan disappear! You are so funny!"
They hugged their mom and thanked her for playing with them. They asked her to show them how she did it. She explained how she unplugged and moved the fan. They learned a new trick and wanted to try it themselves. They took turns making the fan disappear and reappear with the sheet and the plug. They had more fun and laughter with the fan and their mom. They felt comfortable and happy.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to go to the park with their mom. They loved to play on the swings, slide down the slide, and run on the grass. Sometimes, they also got to buy ice cream from the vendor, who was a charming man with a big smile and a colorful cart.
One day, they went to the park and saw the vendor waiting near the gate. They ran to him and asked for ice cream. The vendor said, "Hello, Lily and Ben! What flavor do you want today? I have chocolate, vanilla, and strawberry."
Lily said, "I want chocolate, please." Ben said, "I want vanilla, please." The vendor gave them each a cone with a scoop of ice cream. They thanked him and licked their ice cream happily.
But then, a big dog came running towards them. It was brown and furry, and it barked loudly. Lily and Ben were scared of the dog. They dropped their ice cream and screamed. The dog sniffed their ice cream and ate it. Lily and Ben cried.
The vendor heard their scream and came to help them. He shooed away the dog and hugged them. He said, "Don't worry, Lily and Ben. It's okay. The dog was just hungry and curious. He didn't mean to scare you or take your ice cream. Here, I have more ice cream for you. You can have another cone, or you can share a big cup with two spoons. What do you say?"
Lily and Ben stopped crying and looked at the vendor. They felt sorry for the dog and for wasting their ice cream. They said, "Thank you, vendor. You are very kind. We don't need another cone. We can share a big cup with two spoons. And we can give some to the dog, too. Maybe he will be our friend."
The vendor smiled and said, "That's very nice of you, Lily and Ben. You are very brave and generous. Here, take this big cup of ice cream. It has chocolate, vanilla, and strawberry. You can enjoy it with the dog. And remember, don't scream at animals. They have feelings, too. Be gentle and friendly, and they will be gentle and friendly, too."
Lily and Ben nodded and took the big cup of ice cream. They walked to the dog, who was sitting nearby. They said, "Hello, dog. We are sorry we screamed at you. We were scared. Do you want some ice cream?" The dog wagged his tail and licked their hands. They gave him some ice cream and petted him. They became friends.
Lily and Ben learned a lesson that day. They learned to be kind to animals and to share with others. They also learned to appreciate the vendor, who was a charming man with a big smile and a colorful cart.

Tom and Jen are in a car with Mom and Dad. They are going to visit Grandma in the city. Tom and Jen are bored. They want to play and see new things.
"Are we there yet?" Tom asks.
"Not yet, honey. We have to pass many cars and buildings. Be patient, please," Mom says.
"I don't like cars and buildings. They are noisy and ugly. I want to see trees and flowers and animals," Jen says.
"Me too," Tom says.
They look out the window and see only cars and buildings. They sigh and frown.
Suddenly, they hear a loud honk. A big truck is behind them. It is angry and wants to pass them. It honks again and again.
"Stop honking! You are scaring us!" Tom and Jen shout.
"Sorry, kids. The truck is in a hurry. He is not patient. He is rude," Dad says.
He tries to move to the side, but there is no space. The truck keeps honking and following them.
"What can we do?" Mom asks.
"I have an idea," Tom says. He picks up his toy dinosaur and holds it out the window. He makes it roar and bite the air.
"Look, Jen. A dinosaur! He is our friend. He will scare the truck away," Tom says.
Jen smiles and picks up her toy unicorn. She holds it out the window too. She makes it neigh and sparkle.
"Look, Tom. A unicorn! She is our friend too. She will make the truck happy," Jen says.
The truck driver sees the toys and laughs. He stops honking and waves at them. He passes them with a smile.
"Wow, you did it, kids. You made the truck go away. You are very clever and brave," Mom says.
"Thank you, Mom. We are happy now. We can't wait to see Grandma," Tom and Jen say.
They hug their toys and look out the window again. They see some trees and flowers and animals. They cheer and clap.
The end.

"Can we watch TV?" Ben asked.
Mom shook her head. She said, "No, TV is not good for you. You need to use your imagination and creativity. The board game will help you with that. It will also teach you how to cooperate and take turns. Trust me, you will have fun if you try it."
Lily and Ben sighed. They did not want to make Mom sad. They went to the closet and took out the board game. They opened the box and looked at the board. It had a map of the world with different colors and shapes. It also had cards and dice and tokens.
"What do we do?" Lily asked.
Ben shrugged. He said, "I don't know. Let's read the instructions."
They tried to read the instructions, but they were too hard. They had many big words and numbers and symbols. They did not understand them.
"This is too hard," Lily said. "Let's play something else."
Ben agreed. He said, "Yeah, this is boring. Let's put it away."
They were about to close the box when they heard a voice. It was not Mom's voice. It was a different voice. It came from the board.
"Hello, Lily and Ben," the voice said. "I am the board game. I want to play with you. Don't be afraid. I will teach you how to play. It is easy and fun. You will learn a lot and have a great adventure. Do you want to play with me?"
Lily and Ben were surprised. They looked at each other. They looked at the board. They were curious. They decided to give it a try.
"Okay, board game," Lily said. "We will play with you. But you have to be nice and patient and encouraging. We are still learning."
The board game smiled. It said, "Of course, I will be nice and patient and encouraging. I am your friend. I want you to have fun and grow. Now, let's begin. The first thing you need to do is to choose a token. The token will be your character. You can be anyone you want. You can be a pirate, a princess, a astronaut, a detective, or anything else. What do you want to be?"
Lily and Ben thought for a moment. They picked their tokens. Lily chose a princess. Ben chose a pirate.
"Good choice," the board game said. "Now, let's roll the dice. The dice will tell you how many spaces you can move on the board. The board will take you to different places and times. You will see amazing things and meet interesting people. You will also face challenges and dangers. You will have to use your skills and knowledge and courage to overcome them. You will also have to help each other and work together. Are you ready?"
Lily and Ben nodded. They were no longer bored. They were excited. They rolled the dice and moved their tokens. The board game came to life. It showed them pictures and sounds and stories. It asked them questions and gave them clues and hints. It praised them and encouraged them and cheered them on. It was the best game they ever played. They forgot about the rain and the time and everything else. They only wanted to play more and more.
Mom watched them from the kitchen. She smiled. She was happy. She knew she had given them the best gift ever. A gift that would spark their imagination and creativity. A gift that would teach them how to cooperate and take turns. A gift that would make them laugh and learn and grow. A gift that was not boring at all. A gift that was magical.

Max went to the big tree and found a nice shelter. He was happy and began to rest. Suddenly, there was a loud noise. It was a cat named Whiskers. Whiskers wanted to catch Lily! Max was scared, but he knew he had to help his new friend.
Max barked very loudly to scare Whiskers away. The cat ran away, and Lily was safe. Lily thanked Max for saving her. They both learned that helping each other is important, and they became best friends.
The moral of the story is that friends should help each other, even when it is hard or scary.

The oven was very hot. The heat reached the tray. The dough animals started to feel warm. They started to melt. Their eyes and noses and mouths started to fade. Tina and Tim were playing a game. They each had a box of matches. Tina said to Tim, "Let's see who can match the most matches together." 
Tim replied, "Okay, let's do it." 
They both gathered the matches from their boxes and started matching them. Tina was making fat, vertical stacks of the matches. Tim was making quick motions with his hands, matching the matches faster. 
At the end, Tina said: "Wow, you made more matches than I did. You must be very fast!"
Tim smiled and said, "It's easy when you just make small motions with your hands." 
They both laughed, put away their matches, and decided to play another game.

"Let's go, Ben!" Sam said. "It will be fun!"
"No, Sam," Ben said. "Mom said we can't go there. It is too far and too dangerous. There might be snakes or holes or bad people."
"Mom is not here," Sam said. "She is at the store. She will not know. Come on, Ben, don't be scared."
Sam ran to the hill. Ben followed him. He did not want to be alone. He did not want Sam to be mad at him.
They climbed the hill. It was hard and steep. They slipped and fell many times. They got dirty and hurt. But they did not stop. They wanted to see what was on the other side.
They reached the top of the hill. They looked around. They saw a big road with many cars and trucks. They saw a big sign that said "Danger. Do not cross."
"Wow, look at that!" Sam said. "Let's go and see the cars and trucks. They are so big and fast and loud!"
"No, Sam," Ben said. "We can't go there. It is too dangerous. The sign says so. The cars and trucks might hit us. We might die."
"Ben, you are so boring," Sam said. "You are always afraid of everything. I am not afraid. I am brave. I want to see the cars and trucks. They are so cool!"
Sam ran to the road. Ben tried to stop him. He tried to grab his hand. He tried to yell at him. But Sam was too fast. He was too far. He was too deaf. He did not hear Ben. He did not see the car. He did not feel the pain.
Ben saw the car. He saw Sam. He saw blood. He felt pain. He felt fear. He felt sadness. He screamed and cried. He wished he could prevent this. He wished he could go back. He wished he could say sorry. But it was too late. Sam was gone. Ben was alone.

Then, the little bug drew a big bird. The bird seemed nice at first. But, the bird saw the bug's ink and wanted it for itself. The bird took the ink away from the little bug. The little bug was sad. He did not know what to do.
The bug had an idea. He asked the sun and the flower for help. They all worked together to get the ink back from the bird. The bird saw how well they worked together and felt sorry. The bird gave the ink back to the little bug.
From that day on, the little bug, the sun, the flower, and the bird became good friends. They all drew with the magic ink and made the forest a happy place. The little bug learned that working together is better than being alone.

The worm felt embarrass. He wanted to show the bird that he could do something special too. So, the worm started to wiggle and wiggle. He wiggled through the dirt, making a long tunnel. The tunnel helped the plants grow big and strong.
The bird saw the strong plants and said, "Wow, worm! You did a good job! I am sorry for making you feel embarrass. We can both do special things." The worm and the bird became friends. They learned that everyone has something special they can do, even if they are small or big. And that is the moral of the story: everyone has something special to offer.

He made houses, shops, roads and bridges with his blocks and books. He liked to pretend that he was the driver or the pilot of his vehicles and zoom around his village.
One day, he decided to try something new. He wanted to see what his village would look like if he reversed everything. He took all his vehicles and turned them around, so they faced the opposite way. He moved his blocks and books, so they made different shapes and colors. He even swapped his bed and his closet, so his room looked different.
He was very proud of his reversed village and wanted to show his mom. He ran to the door and called, "Mom, mom, come and see what I made!" But when he opened the door, he was surprised. His mom was not there. Instead, he saw a big dog with a wagging tail and a friendly face. The dog barked and licked Tom's face.
Tom was confused. He wondered where his mom was and why there was a dog in his house. He looked around and saw that everything outside his room was also reversed. The furniture, the pictures, the plants, everything was in the wrong place. He realized that he had not only reversed his village, but his whole house!
He was scared and wanted to go back to normal. He quickly ran back to his room and reversed everything again. He turned his vehicles, his blocks, his books, his bed and his closet back to the way they were before. He hoped that his house would also go back to normal.
He opened the door again and sighed with relief. His mom was there, smiling and holding a cake. She said, "Happy birthday, Tom! I have a surprise for you. I brought you a new friend. Meet Rover, your new dog!" Tom was happy and hugged his mom and his dog. He realized that his reversed village was just a silly game, but his new dog was a real gift. He thanked his mom and invited her to see his village. He decided to keep his village the way it was, but he also made room for Rover's bed and bowl. He thought that his village was more fun with a dog. He was a creative boy who liked to make things with his toys.

Tom was a fox who liked to play in the mud. He did not like to clean his fur or his paws. He thought it was a waste of time and he wanted to have fun.
One day, he saw a big puddle near the forest. He ran to it and jumped in. He splashed and rolled and laughed. He was very happy.
But then he heard a voice. It was his mother. She was looking for him. She saw him in the puddle and she was upset.
"Tom, what are you doing?" she asked. "You are all dirty and wet. You need to clean yourself right now. Come with me."
Tom did not want to go. He wanted to stay in the puddle. He said, "No, Mom. I like the mud. It is fun. I do not want to clean."
His mother was angry. She said, "Tom, you are being naughty. You have to clean yourself. It is good for you. If you do not clean, you will get sick and itch. And you will smell bad. And no one will want to play with you. Do you want that?"
Tom thought for a moment. He did not want to get sick or itch. He did not want to smell bad. He did not want to lose his friends. He realized his mother was right. He said, "Sorry, Mom. You are right. I do not want that. I will clean myself."
His mother smiled. She said, "That's a good boy. Come on, let's go to the river. I will help you clean. And then we can have some lunch. And maybe later, we can play some more. But not in the mud, OK?"
Tom nodded. He followed his mother to the river. He washed his fur and his paws. He felt fresh and clean. He thanked his mother. He said, "I love you, Mom. And I love to clean."
His mother hugged him. She said, "I love you too, Tom. And I am proud of you. You learned a good lesson today. Cleaning is not a waste of time. It is a way to take care of yourself and others. And it can be fun too."
The moral of the story is: Cleaning is important for your health and happiness. And listening to your parents is wise.

Tom nodded. He thought he knew everything. He was ignorant. He did not listen to his mom. He ran to the corn field and grabbed the first corn he saw. It was brown and rotten. He did not notice the smell or the bugs. He peeled the husk and took a big bite.

He threw the corn away and ran back to his mom. He was crying and holding his mouth.

"Tom, I'm sorry you ate the rotten corn. You should have listened to me. I tried to teach you how to choose the good corn. The rotten corn can make you sick. You have to be careful and look and smell before you eat. Do you understand?" she said.
Tom nodded. He was sorry too. He learned his lesson. He was not ignorant anymore. He wanted to be smart and careful. He said sorry to his mom and thanked her for the water. He did not want to eat corn anymore. He wanted to see the animals again. He hoped they did not eat the rotten corn too. He hoped they were happy and healthy. He loved the farm and his mom.
